meta.title: Two Emails, Two Places
meta.textType: functional: two emails on one topic, to compare

paragraphs: On Tuesday, December twenty-second, Lily, Mia, and Leo sat at the library computer. Teacher Kim gave them a job. "Read two emails about a weekend place," she said. "Then tell me what is the same and what is different." Ravi was Leo's pen pal, and Nadia was Mia's pen pal. The first subject line was "My weekend at the hill park." The second subject line was "My weekend at the beach club." Leo read the first email out loud.

"Dear Leo, on Saturday my family went to the hill park." "It is a nature area with fresh air." "We had a barbecue under a big tree." "After lunch, I rode a pony for twenty minutes." "It is a quiet place, because only a few people go there." "In summer, the park has a camp for children." "Best wishes, Ravi." Leo drew a green hill, a big tree, a barbecue grill with smoke, and a small brown pony.

Then Mia read the second email. "Dear Mia, on Sunday my family went to the beach club." "We rented a small boat, and I tried sailing." "I also watched people go surfing and diving." "Actually, it was my first time on a boat." "It is a busy place, because many families go there." "There is a boat festival there every year." "Best wishes, Nadia." Mia drew a sandy beach with a boat, a surfboard, and a diving mask. Lily made a page with two columns. The columns said "Ravi's park" and "Nadia's club." Lily wrote a short list in each column.

"Ravi's park is not as busy as Nadia's club," said Lily. "The beach club is too busy for me," said Leo. "Both places are outdoors, and both have a lot of fun things to do," said Mia. "Ravi's family had a barbecue, but Nadia's family rented a boat," said Lily. Teacher Kim looked at the page and smiled. "Good work," she said. "You found the same things and the different things."

"Which place is bigger?" asked Leo. "The emails do not say, so we can ask," said Lily. Leo opened a new email and wrote two questions. "Dear Ravi, how big is the hill park?" "Is the pony friendly?" "Best wishes, Leo."
text.summary: Teacher Kim asks Lily, Mia, and Leo to compare two emails about a weekend place. Ravi writes about a quiet hill park, and Nadia writes about a busy beach club.
